verdict_word: A penny beat, 16% growth, and the biggest infrastructure fund ever on the way
takeaways: Total distributable earnings were $1.72 billion ($0.73 a share), including $222 million of realized carried interest, per the company release.
Asset management fee-related earnings rose 15%; wealth solutions (insurance) earnings rose 22%, with insurance assets near $200 billion.
After quarter-end, Brookfield got $13 billion more for its infrastructure flagship, $26 billion committed so far; it says the fund will become 'by far, the largest infrastructure fund ever raised.'
About $300 million of stock bought back since the last report, almost $900 million this year.
verdict: Brookfield owns the toll roads, pipes and power plants the AI boom has to plug into, and it collects fees on top. A one-cent beat is boring, and boring is the point.
